The bridge E edges out the hub C, 0.159 to 0.156, ahead of D 0.147, while the pendant G, behind a single edge, scores 0.070." width="100%"} Closeness centrality uses shortest-path distances; current-flow closeness uses *effective resistance* instead, treating each edge as a resistor (Brandes & Fleischer 2005). The effective resistance between two nodes is small when they are joined by many short, parallel routes, so it accounts for every path rather than only the shortest. The score is the reciprocal of a node's total effective resistance to all others. It is the same measure as Stephenson & Zelen's *information centrality*, which NetworkX also exposes as `information_centrality()`. Edge weights act as conductances (higher weight, lower resistance). The graph must be undirected and connected. For the resistances themselves, see `resistance_distance_matrix()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"current_flow_closeness_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub of a star is electrically closest to everyone: ::: {#a7326e60 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) scores = star.current_flow_closeness_centrality(return_dict=True) {n: round(s, 3) for n, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 0.25, 2: 0.143, 3: 0.143, 4: 0.143, 5: 0.143} ``` ::: :::
